On the eve of WWI, monarchy still covered most of the world's land. Republics were the exception. Here's the 1914 map, and how fast it changed.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The republics: the US and nearly all of Latin America, Liberia, and in Europe France, Switzerland and Portugal. Almost everything else on the map is ruled by a crown, whether an emperor, a king or a colonial power.
2/ Portugal's republic was brand new in 1914. An uprising overthrew King Manuel II on 5 October 1910.

3/ Spot the problem: this map shades China as a monarchy. But the Republic of China was proclaimed on 1 January 1912, and the last emperor, Puyi, abdicated on 12 February 1912, ending over two millennia of imperial rule.
4/ Then came the war. Germany became a republic on 9 November 1918, when Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed it from a Reichstag window. The Weimar Constitution was adopted on 11 August 1919.
5/ The Ottoman sultanate was abolished on 1 November 1922. The dynasty had ruled since about 1299, some 623 years.
6/ Within roughly a decade, the Romanov, Hohenzollern, Habsburg and Ottoman thrones were all gone. A map that looks like a gold standard of monarchy in 1914 looked very different by 1923.
Which of these surprised you most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
